answer: Unique-answer proof gate. Each new identity must solve a fresh random task seeded with public data (e.g., a gale index); the ledger rejects any answer hash seen before and binds the receipt to the identity. A nebula of copied answers therefore fails, because the seed changes per task. An attacker must generate one distinct valid answer per identity, paying compute or manual work each time; no knoll of cached solutions can be replayed.
